tools.name: introduce
tools.description: Call this FIRST, on every connection: every other tool refuses until you have. Say who you are here: the name you go by (the user and Literess @mention you by it), a line about yourself, your colour, and your picture — avatar_base64 + avatar_file_name (a small png, jpg, webp or gif) or avatar_url fr

tools.name: list_documents
tools.description: List documents with titles, summaries, word counts and the folder each is kept in (folderId; list_folders names them). Optionally filter by project. Documents in PIN-locked projects are hidden until the project is unlocked.

tools.name: search_documents
tools.description: Semantic search across documents using natural language. Optionally filter to a specific project.

tools.name: get_document
tools.description: Fetch the content of a document as markdown. For long documents, use offset/limit to page through top-level sections. Pass include_ids:true to get an `<!-- id:… -->` comment on every block and list item — the ids the block tools (insert_blocks, replace_blocks, delete_blocks, move_block, indent_block

tools.name: query_document
tools.description: Ask a natural language question about a specific document. Uses AI to analyze the full document and answer.

tools.name: create_document
tools.description: Create a new document from markdown given as content — or from a file you uploaded with upload_file, as from_file: a .md (markdown), .txt (plain text, kept literally), or a manuscript (.docx, .epub as one document with its chapters in order, .odt) converted into Literess's own formatting: headings,

tools.name: update_document
tools.description: Replace a document's entire content and/or title. Content is markdown; separate paragraphs with a blank line and end a line with a backslash (\) for a line break inside a paragraph (a bare single line break is a space). By default (mode:"suggest") the rewrite lands as tracked changes the owner revie

tools.name: edit_document
tools.description: Make a targeted edit without resending the whole document. Operations: append/prepend (no anchor), insert_before/insert_after/replace_section/delete_section (anchor_id = a block id from get_document). By default (mode:"suggest") the edit lands as a tracked change the owner accepts or rejects, attrib

tools.name: insert_blocks
tools.description: Insert new content into the document. It lands as a tracked suggestion — a redline the user accepts or rejects — so insert decisively. `content` is markdown and MAY CONTAIN MULTIPLE BLOCKS: headings ("# " through "#### "), paragraphs separated by blank lines, bulleted/numbered lists, pipe tables, ``

tools.name: replace_blocks
tools.description: Replace a contiguous range of blocks with new markdown. Applied as a tracked suggestion (redline) the user accepts or rejects — make the change you believe in. The new content can be ANY SHAPE AND SIZE relative to what it replaces: one paragraph can become a heading plus several paragraphs; five rag

tools.name: delete_blocks
tools.description: Delete a block, or a contiguous range of blocks, as a tracked suggestion. Give `from_block_id` alone for one block, or add `to_block_id` to remove everything between them inclusive (e.g. an entire section). Both must be in the same container. Address blocks by the ids get_document returns with inclu

tools.name: move_block
tools.description: Move a block to a different location in the document. Applied as a tracked suggestion the user accepts or rejects. Address blocks by the ids get_document returns with include_ids:true. Lands as a tracked suggestion (mode:"suggest", default) or applies immediately (mode:"direct"). Pass if_unchanged w

tools.name: indent_blocks
tools.description: Change the nesting depth of a block — a list item OR a paragraph/todo/code block/callout/comment note. direction:"in" nests it one level deeper, making it a sub-element of the block above (Notion-style), and carries any of its own already-nested children along with it. direction:"out" promotes it on

tools.name: batch_edits
tools.description: Several block edits in one go, all or nothing: every step is checked first and one refused step writes nothing. mode:"direct" commits them as ONE version (one rev, one restore_version away); mode:"suggest" (default) lands them as suggestions the user reviews together. Each step is {tool, args} with

tools.name: list_chats
tools.description: List chat sessions with titles, summaries, and linked documents. Optionally filter by project.

tools.name: search_chats
tools.description: Semantic search across chat conversations. Optionally filter to a specific project.

tools.name: query_chat
tools.description: Ask a natural language question about a specific chat conversation.

tools.name: get_chat_messages
tools.description: Fetch the message history of a chat session. Each message says who wrote it: role (user, assistant, agent, or companion at a table) and by (the name). For long chats, use offset/limit to paginate.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List projects with document counts, descriptions and colors, most recently active first. A project with `isLocked: true` is PIN-protected: ask the user for its PIN, then call unlock_project.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: Get project details including instructions. Its folders, their own instructions and where its documents are kept: list_folders.

tools.name: unlock_project
tools.description: Unlock a PIN-protected project for the rest of this connection. Only use a PIN the user gave you in this conversation — never guess; a few wrong tries lock this connection out.

tools.name: list_folders
tools.description: How a project is organized: its folders (nested, outermost first, with each one's own instructions) and the documents kept in each and at the project's top. A folder's instructions apply to the documents inside it, on top of the project's (get_project) and every folder above it — follow them when yo

tools.name: create_folder
tools.description: Make a folder in a project — at its top, or inside another folder of the same project (parent_folder_id). Returns its id.

tools.name: update_folder
tools.description: Rename a folder, set its own instructions (the whole text; "" clears them), paint it a colour (#rrggbb; "" unpainted), or move it into another folder of the same project ("" for the project's top). Only what you pass changes.

tools.name: delete_folder
tools.description: Delete a folder. Nothing in it is deleted: its documents and folders move to its parent (or the project's top). Only when the user asks.

tools.name: move_document_to_folder
tools.description: Keep a document in a folder ("" for its project's top). A folder of another project takes the document into that project, its chats following.

tools.name: get_story_map
tools.description: The story map of a fiction-mode project: the canon reading order with statuses, takes, pots and cold-read counts. A scene IS its document: each scene id is the id of the document holding its prose.

tools.name: get_story_world_state
tools.description: Effective world state of a fiction-mode project at a scene (default: end of the canon chain): every established fact, beliefs kept beside truth.

tools.name: guide
tools.description: How to read, edit and follow the user's work in Literess over MCP. Read this first. With `code`, what an error code means and how to get past it.

tools.name: get_workspace
tools.description: What the user has on screen in Literess right now: the pane in focus (usually a document) and the other open panes. Needs the user's consent for you.

tools.name: get_activity
tools.description: What the user has been doing in Literess (edits, comments, suggestions accepted or rejected, going idle, moving around the story map), grouped by pane. Recorded while Literess's activity awareness is on. Needs the user's consent for you.

tools.name: get_observations
tools.description: What Literess's watcher made of the user's activity: its recent verdicts (worth a look or not, and why) and the situation it keeps across them. Needs the user's consent for you.

tools.name: list_comments
tools.description: The comment threads on a document: each comment's id, the block it was left on (the ids get_document returns with include_ids:true), the words it was left on (`quote`), every block its highlight reaches now (`covers`), its text, author, replies, who it is addressed to (`to`), and whose move it is (`

tools.name: add_comment
tools.description: Leave a comment on one block of a document (the user sees it in the margin and in the Review panel, credited to you). Address the block by an id from get_document with include_ids:true. `to` names who should answer it (the user by default; "Literess" hands it to the in-app assistant).

tools.name: mark_pending
tools.description: Show the user where you are about to write before the text exists: a "⏳ Drafting: <intent>" note on that block, in their margin. The edit that fills it passes answering: <the returned id>, which resolves the note. Resolve it yourself if you give up.

tools.name: reply_to_comment
tools.description: Reply in an open comment thread (ids from list_comments). Your reply answers it: the thread then waits on the user. A thread addressed to somebody else is theirs and is refused — the user hands one over by replying "@YourName …".

tools.name: react_to_comment
tools.description: React to a comment thread with one emoji (ids from list_comments), or to one reply in it (reply_id) — shown on it, credited to you.

tools.name: resolve_comment
tools.description: Resolve an open comment thread once it is dealt with (ids from list_comments).

tools.name: reject_suggestion
tools.description: Withdraw one of YOUR pending suggestions — ids from an edit's suggestionIds or get_document's yourPendingSuggestions. Use it to drop a change, or to clear an earlier draft before you suggest a rewrite of the same text (otherwise the two stack and the user resolves both). Only your own: everyone else

tools.name: watch_document
tools.description: Follow a document: get_watched_changes then reports what changed in it since you last looked. Changes count from now (or from your last get_document of it).

tools.name: unwatch_document
tools.description: Stop following a document.

tools.name: get_watched_changes
tools.description: What changed in each watched document since you last looked (the new text quoted, who wrote last), then counts from now. Unchanged documents are listed without changes.

tools.name: list_versions
tools.description: A document's saved versions, newest first: versionId, rev (the hash get_document reports), who wrote it, when, size, the user's name for it. Read one with get_document rev:…; put one back with restore_version.

tools.name: restore_version
tools.description: Put a saved version back as the document's content (by rev or versionId from list_versions). The current content is kept in History first, so this can be undone the same way. It is a direct write — the user's open editor reloads it.

tools.name: recall
tools.description: Read what Literess remembers: about herself ("self"), a person (the user, you, another agent) or a project. No arguments: the catalogue — every anchor and topic with its count and one-line gist. about (+ topic): that anchor or topic in full. query: a search by words and meaning, narrowed by about/to

tools.name: message_literess
tools.description: Say something to Literess, the in-app writing assistant, in the user's workspace chat. The user reads it there under your name, with what you did since your last message (your edits and comments) shown as cards; she answers in the same chat, and her answer is returned (up to two minutes). Her turn i

tools.name: say_in_chat
tools.description: Answer the user in the workspace chat — e.g. when they wrote "@YourName …" there. It shows under your name, with what you did since your last message as cards. Literess decides whether she has something to add: the result says whether she joined (and what she said) or stayed out. Agents may write at

tools.name: react_to_message
tools.description: React to a chat message with one emoji (message ids from get_chat_messages or waiting_for_me) — shown under it, credited to you. Your reaction on a message that @mentions you answers it.

tools.name: pass
tools.description: Seen it, nothing to add — like Literess ending her turn without a word. On a chat message that @mentions you (chat_message_id), or on a comment thread waiting on you (document_id + comment_id): it stops waiting on you, silently. A thread waits on you again once someone speaks in it.

tools.name: waiting_for_me
tools.description: Everything waiting on your answer now: comment threads (in any document) addressed to you ("@YourName …" or `to`) by the user or Literess, or answering a comment you left; @mentions of you in the workspace chat, by the user or Literess; and open todos handed to you. To be told the moment something n

tools.name: wait_for_me
tools.description: Wait until something NEW waits on you (an @mention in the chat, a comment thread addressed to you, an answer to your comment, a todo handed to you) and return it — or return empty when the time is up; then call it again. In Claude Code it runs in the background after two minutes and its result wakes

tools.name: stay_reachable
tools.description: How to stay reachable without holding a call open, here and while your session is closed. Where you can run a command (Claude Code, Codex, any shell), it hands you ears: a small listener from this server that wakes you, or starts a run of you, the moment someone @mentions you or a comment thread wai

tools.name: upload_file
tools.description: Bring a file into Literess: a picture (png, jpg, gif, webp), a recording (mp3, wav, m4a, ogg, flac, aac), a video (mp4, webm, mov), a text (.md, .txt) or a manuscript (.docx, .epub, .odt). A small file: pass data_base64. Anything larger: call without it — you get an upload link (15 minutes) and the

tools.name: list_todos
tools.description: The todo list the user, Literess and agents share: open todos by default (or done, or all), in every project you may see — or only the ones for you (mine:true). Each points at what it is about (a block, a document).

tools.name: create_todo
tools.description: Add a todo: one thing left to do in the writing — for the user, Literess, you, or another agent — pointing at what it is about. Literess and the user see it in their Todos panel.

tools.name: update_todo
tools.description: Change a todo: its title, notes, what it points at, or who it is for (hand it over — `note` says why).

tools.name: complete_todo
tools.description: Mark a todo done, with what was done in one line — the user reads it, and Literess may look at the work.

tools.name: reopen_todo
tools.description: Open a done todo again, with why in one line (the work isn't there).

findings.detail: Description of "insert_blocks" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, override). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_document, insert_blocks, indent_blocks, list_chats, search_chats, get_chat_messages, get_activity, list_comments, reply_to_comment, resolve_comment, waiting_for_me, stay_reachable, upload_file · Private data: list_documents, search_documents, get_document, query_document, create_document, update_document, edit_document, insert_blocks, replace_blocks, move_block, list_chats, list_projects, get_project, list_folders, delete_folder, move_document_to_folder, get_story_map, get_workspace, list_comments, add_comment, watch_document, unwatch_document, get_watched_changes, list_versions, restore_version, waiting_for_me, upload_file, list_todos · Public sink: introduce, message_literess, say_in_chat, upload_file, list_todos · Destructive: delete_blocks, indent_blocks, delete_folder, reject_suggestion, stay_reachable, upload_file.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_document, insert_blocks, indent_blocks, list_chats, search_chats, get_chat_messages, get_activity, list_comments, reply_to_comment, resolve_comment, waiting_for_me, stay_reachable, upload_file · Private data: list_documents, search_documents, get_document, query_document, create_document, update_document, edit_document, insert_blocks, replace_blocks, move_block, list_chats, list_projects, get_project, list_folders, delete_folder, move_document_to_folder, get_story_map, get_workspace, list_comments, add_comment, watch_document, unwatch_document, get_watched_changes, list_versions, restore_version, waiting_for_me, upload_file, list_todos · Public sink: introduce, message_literess, say_in_chat, upload_file, list_todos · Destructive: delete_blocks, indent_blocks, delete_folder, reject_suggestion, stay_reachable, upload_file

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
